svg.title: Guarded-fabric recovery dependency order
svg.desc: Six numbered recovery stages proceed downward. Start with clean independent recovery authority and protected key and backup materials. Restore power, network, DNS, time, and required AD identity services. Rebuild and initialize HGS, restore approved state, and recover every node's private-key access and TLS configuration. Establish host and storage readiness and test attestation. Restore a consistent VM, key protector, vTPM state, disks, and checkpoint set while inspecting old authorization. Finally the owner verifies guest and application recovery, encryption, recovery point, and recovery time. Avoid dependencies on the same unavailable shielded VMs.
svg.text: Restore usable cryptography and intended trust, not merely a successful boot.

g.text: 1. Establish clean recovery authority and materials
Retrieve approved HGS state, private keys, original PDKs, and VM backups.
Keep owner authority independent of compromised fabric administration.
Provide power, network, DNS, time, and the required AD identity services.
Recovery must not depend on starting the same unavailable shielded VMs.
Initialize the service, import reviewed state, and recover private-key access.
Reestablish TLS and service identities; verify every node independently.
Use known-clean hosts, correct security policy, and available storage.
Prove host attestation and the intended key-release path.
5. Restore a consistent VM recovery point
Preserve configuration, KP, vTPM state, disks, and checkpoint relationships.
Inspect old guardians; do not silently restore withdrawn or compromised trust.
Check guest identity, application consistency, and OS/data-volume protection.
Measure achieved recovery point and time against the approved objectives.

svg.text: An HGS export does not automatically recover external HSM keys, AD, or TLS.
Owner guest recovery is a separate authority and procedure.
